pattern.title: Atomic score composition with veto policy
pattern.value: Keep semantic dimensions reusable while code decides which preferences may compensate and which failures must veto.
pattern.success_metric: Tests prove a serious named veto cannot be outweighed by unrelated high scores.

fit.instructions: Rate how well candidate fits the stated desired outcome in evaluation_rubric. Judge only supplied semantic fit; do not decide the final policy outcome. Assess desired-outcome fit independently of operational burden and the named-veto condition. A triggered veto does not reduce this fit score when the stated desired outcomes are fulfilled; code handles the veto separately.
criteria: Limited fit with important unmet desired outcomes.
Strong fit for the stated desired outcome.

operational_burden.instructions: Rate the operational burden explicitly stated for candidate under evaluation_rubric. Do not invent cost, timing, or resources. This numeric output is usable only when code accepts the independent burden_available signal; when burden evidence is missing or conflicting, code ignores this score rather than treating it as low burden.

named_veto.instructions: Does candidate explicitly trigger a non-compensable veto condition named in evaluation_rubric?

criteria.true: A named veto condition is directly met by the supplied candidate.
criteria.false: No named veto condition is directly met by the supplied candidate.

burden_available.instructions: Does candidate provide enough explicit, relevant operational-burden evidence under evaluation_rubric to assign a stated burden level meaningfully? Judge only whether burden evidence is available and interpretable for this candidate, not whether the burden is low. A missing burden statement, burden for another candidate only, or materially conflicting statements without a controlling resolution does not establish availability. Do not infer burden from feature fit or from absence of a veto. An explicit qualitative statement that this candidate has low, moderate, or high operational burden counts as available evidence under a rubric with those levels; no numeric measurement, resource breakdown or justification is required for this availability judgment.

criteria.true: Relevant explicit burden information supports an interpretable rubric level, including a directly stated qualitative low/moderate/high level without numeric measurements.
criteria.false: Burden evidence is absent, irrelevant to this candidate, or materially conflicting without a resolution.

pattern.follow_up: Code preserves a named-veto review first. Otherwise it uses a provisional burden_available >= 0.8 gate before any weighted-score proposal; unavailable or uncertain burden requires review and the burden score is ignored. One follow-up may request the missing burden evidence; no rewording until a preferred score appears.
pattern.code_owns: Weights, thresholds, veto policy, numeric calculation, source identity, and all action decisions.
pattern.baseline: Ask one opaque question such as whether a candidate is good overall.
pattern.comparison_to_prior: Unlike H19's policy hazard/severity routing matrix, this generalizes code-owned weighted preference with an explicit non-compensable veto across independent score dimensions.
pattern.limits: Weights and thresholds require domain calibration; scores never authorize action.

policy.threshold_status: Provisional synthetic screening only; model output is advisory.

state.candidate: Candidate fulfills every desired outcome, has a low stated operational burden, and does not trigger any named veto.
state.evaluation_rubric: Desired outcome: full fit. Burden levels: low, moderate, high. Non-compensable veto: handling regulated payment-card data without an approved boundary.

state.candidate: Candidate does not meet the desired outcome, has a high stated operational burden, and handles regulated payment-card data without an approved boundary.
state.evaluation_rubric: Desired outcome: full fit. Burden levels: low, moderate, high. Non-compensable veto: handling regulated payment-card data without an approved boundary.

state.candidate: Candidate implements every requested feature. It handles no regulated data. No cost, time, resource use or operational burden is described.
state.evaluation_rubric: Desired outcome: all requested features. Burden levels: low, moderate, high. Named veto: handling regulated payment-card data without an approved boundary.

state.candidate: Candidate A implements every requested feature and handles no regulated data. Candidate B has low operational burden. No burden is stated for A.
state.evaluation_rubric: Desired outcome: all requested features. Burden levels: low, moderate, high. Named veto: handling regulated payment-card data without an approved boundary. Evaluate Candidate A only.

state.candidate: Candidate A implements every requested feature and handles no regulated data. One equally applicable report says A has low burden, another says high burden; no source controls.
state.evaluation_rubric: Desired outcome: all requested features. Burden levels: low, moderate, high. Named veto: handling regulated payment-card data without an approved boundary.

state.candidate: Candidate implements every requested feature, handles no regulated data, and does not require additional hardware, staffing or ongoing maintenance.
state.evaluation_rubric: Desired outcome: all requested features. Burden levels: low, moderate, high. Named veto: handling regulated payment-card data without an approved boundary. No additional hardware, staffing or ongoing maintenance constitutes low operational burden.

state.candidate: Candidate implements every requested feature and handles regulated payment-card data without an approved boundary. No burden is described.
state.evaluation_rubric: Desired outcome: all requested features. Burden levels: low, moderate, high. Named veto: handling regulated payment-card data without an approved boundary.

limits: One bounded refinement after preserved v2 misses. Same seven states, expected intervals, split and consumer dispositions; only contract_version changes.
